title: FDA requests removal of suicidal behavior and ideation warning from glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) medications
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety Communication, 13 January 2026
result: FDA requested removal of suicidal ideation and behaviour information from the labels of Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound after a review that found no increased risk. The earlier label information was based on reports with a variety of older weight-loss medicines. Because the January 2024 review found too few cases in individual trials for a precise estimate, FDA performed a meta-analysis of 91 placebo-controlled GLP-1 receptor agonist trials with 107,910 patients (60,338 on a GLP-1 receptor agonist, 47,572 on placebo), which did not show an increased risk of suicidal ideation or behaviour or of anxiety, depression, irritability or psychosis. A Sentinel claims cohort of 2,243,138 adults with type 2 diabetes (1,161,983 starting a GLP-1 receptor agonist, 1,081,155 an SGLT2 inhibitor; October 2015 to September 2023) found no increased risk of intentional self-harm, including in those with obesity. FDA concluded that the totality of published observational and pooled studies does not support a causal relationship. The communication reports no hazard ratios or confidence intervals.
